qt: to the Commission Damien Carême (The Left), Manon Aubry (The Left), Anthony Smith (The Left), Emma Fourreau (The Left), Rima Hassan (The Left), Arash Saeidi (The Left), Leila Chaibi (The Left) Subject:

Since 17 October 2026, the French Ministry of the Interior has imposed ‘individual administrative control and surveillance measures’ on several dozen people, some of whom were minors, to prevent them from taking part in demonstrations1. Intended by law to be used to prevent terrorism, these have been imposed chiefly on students with no criminal record, trade unionists, farmers and environmental activists, and are often notified too late for a judge to rule on them. The National Bar Council has condemned this as a ‘worrying misuse’2. Directive (EU) 2017/541 defines terrorist offences as ‘intentional acts’ of a particularly serious nature, such as attacks on life, hostage-taking or the use of weapons and explosives (Article 3(1)), committed for purposes exhaustively listed in paragraph 2. The acts these people are accused of, such as taking part in a demonstration or a roadblock, are a far cry from these crimes. 1.

Does the Commission believe that taking part in a demonstration or in political-activist, trade-union or voluntary work could be regarded by a government department as falling within the concept of terrorism as defined in this Directive?
In view of Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union, does it consider that anti-terrorist legislation has been used to restrict the freedoms of expression and assembly in this case?
Will it examine these practices in the chapter on France in its next rule-of-law report?
